issue.title: usage: TestSummaryInvalidatesSameStampPrice fails under load (filememo trusts the stamp once it is 2s old)
issue.body:
`TestSummaryInvalidatesSameStampPrice` (internal/usage/summary_cache_test.go) fails under load. Seen in a full `go test -timeout 45m ./...` at 717b69f78 (load ~350 on 14 cores), and again with `-count=20 -run TestSummaryInvalidatesSameStampPrice ./internal/usage` (1 of 20 red at load ~505). At e44b9aef3 it passed 40 of 40 when the load was lower.

```
--- FAIL: TestSummaryInvalidatesSameStampPrice (2.32s)
    summary_cache_test.go:65: direct failed coarse-stamp guard: usage.Totals{Calls:1, Errors:0, Retried:0, Loops:0, Input:1000000, Output:0, CacheRead:0, CacheWrite:0, CacheWrite1h:0, Reasoning:0, Cost:2, Unpriced:0, Credits:0, Credited:0, Timed:0, TTFT:0, DecodeMs:0, DecodeOut:0, DecodeN:0, FloorOut:0, FloorMs:0, FloorN:0}
FAIL	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/usage	64.174s
```
(Other reds from the same test, at 717b69f78 with -count=10: 17.78s and 5.98s.)

Likely cause, from reading the code (not confirmed by injecting the delay yet): the test saves a price of 2, reads it, then saves 4 (a file of the same size) and sets the mtime back to the first save's. `filememo.Read` (internal/filememo/filememo.go) keeps the raw bytes to compare only while the file's mtime is less than `settled` (2s) old. After that it trusts mtime plus size. When more than 2s pass between the first save and the direct `summarize` (each red run took ≥2.3s), the memo returns the cached settings with price 2. So the test depends on finishing within 2s of wall-clock time. Either the test should hold the clock filememo reads, or it should do its two saves close enough together that the guard is what's being tested and not the runner's speed.

Found while verifying the Routing story fix (碳碳双键 on Discord). That change touches no Go code.

comments.body:
Fixed on a fork branch: `fix/2761-filememo-clock-seam` (head `de2c6563`, on upstream `6eb510f7`) — the stamp's age is read by a clock a test can hold.

**Root cause.** `internal/filememo/filememo.go`'s settle and held guards compared `time.Since` against the machine's clock, so a run that took longer than the 2s window between two reads of one file trusted the coarse stamp and served the parse from before the write — the flake `TestSummaryInvalidatesSameStampPrice` saw under load.

**Change.** the guards read a package clock (`filememo.Now`), and the test pins it, so the file's real mtime stops being the thing that decides; the byte-compare guard stays in charge within the settle window however loaded the machine is.

**Verified.** Red: `a temporary 2.5s sleep between the two reads (NOT committed), on base filememo` → `summary_cache_test.go:66: direct failed coarse-stamp guard … Cost:2`
Green: `the same sleep with the seam → `ok`; the committed test pins the clock and the package's tests pass` → `ok github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/usage`

The sleep is the flake made deterministic, so it is not in the committed test; the pin is.

Full `go test -tags nogui ./...` over round 27's branches: 70 packages ok, 5 red (edit `TestWriteAtomicReadOnlyHardLink`, gateway's five, plugin `TestPluginSOCKSProxy`, provider's synctest fatal in `TestUnreadLoginsWriteErrorsKeepCredentials`, testenv `TestProgram`) — every one of them reproduces identically at base `6eb510f7` in this environment (umask 0027), so none is from this change.

Branch: https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/2761-filememo-clock-seam — no PR opened, this repo takes no external PRs; say the word if you'd rather have the patch inline here.
